**PROCESS_VERSION 1** · PR #682 · 2026-11-10

The baseline. It brings in every process change merged so far, including today's:
- `needs-maintainer` (yellow) review label for PRs that are read but not built (#459).
- `P?` label: a paused issue is never picked up, claimed or re-prioritised (#552).
- A fork syncs product code only at release tags; process files sync every session (#562, this PR).
- The `PR-reviewer` agent sets one review label, works in `.claude/worktrees/`, and runs tests in the foreground (#508).
- `review-prs` posts an estimated token cost when a PR turns merge-ready (#680).
- This version mechanism (#682).

**What a fork must do now:** pull the process files once by hand (the command in this issue's body). From then on, your agent checks `PROCESS_VERSION` at the start of each session and pulls future changes itself.

@mkinney @austin62jake @seelesturm @tbrasselle - you're the current contributors working from forks. Please subscribe to this issue, so you're notified when the process changes.

**PROCESS_VERSION 2** · PR #683 · 2026-11-10 - wording only: AGENTS.md's fork rule now says process files are the one exception to "never into the fork's main"; the release-notes step reads as a plain sentence. **Fork action:** pull the process files (the command in this issue's body), or let your agent's session-start check do it.

**PROCESS_VERSION 3** · PR #685 · 2026-11-10

- **New project skill `/resolve-conflicts`** (`.claude/skills/resolve-conflicts/`):
  - **Contributor mode** (`/resolve-conflicts [login]`): merges main into your conflicting PRs (never rebase or force-push), keeps both sides of additive conflicts, takes main's snapshot PNGs and changelog files, runs the targeted gate, pushes, and comments "ready for a re-check". If both sides changed the same logic, it stops and reports.
  - **Maintainer mode** (`/resolve-conflicts check`): re-checks every `conflicts` PR and restores `merge-ready` or routes it to a review.
- **AGENTS.md, Autonomous Work Law:** conflicting PRs are re-merged by their author, and the maintainer re-checks. Fork agents run contributor mode at the start of each session, after the process-file sync.

**Fork action:** pull the process files (the command in this issue's body). Then run `/resolve-conflicts` on your open PRs: 18 of yesterday's merge-ready PRs now conflict with main after the latest merges.

**PROCESS_VERSION 4** · PR #687 · 2026-11-10 - `/resolve-conflicts` refinements: a PR still marked ready (anyone's) goes back to draft before the merge-of-main push, and the maintainer's delta review may set any review label, including `needs-maintainer`. **Fork action:** pull the process files, or let your agent's session-start check do it.

The camcraft-mcp skill's quotes of the rule name both labels. · **Forks:** sync process files (`git checkout upstream/main -- AGENTS.md .claude/agents .claude/skills .claude/PROCESS_VERSION scripts/gate.ps1 scripts/gate.sh`), and label new `MCP:` issues `P1` + `area:mcp`.

`PROCESS_VERSION 6` · PR #747 · AGENTS.md Issue Law "Every issue is weighted by effort":
- **Labels:** one `effort:low|medium|high|max` label per issue, set when the issue is filed. The labels exist now.
- **Safety floor:** G-code, collision/gouge checks, stock simulation, geometry and every P0 are at least `effort:high`.
- **Workers:** issues are worked by `.claude/agents/issue-worker-<effort>.md` (haiku / sonnet / opus / fable) through the new `/work-issue` skill.
- **Reviews:** they run at least on the medium tier, and on high under the safety floor.
- **Escalation:** two failed quick gates, or work bigger than the label, raises the label one step and releases the issue. Only the maintainer lowers a label.
- **Costs:** the `review-prs` cost comment records the effort and any escalation.

**Forks:** sync process files (`git checkout upstream/main -- AGENTS.md .claude/agents .claude/skills .claude/PROCESS_VERSION scripts/gate.ps1 scripts/gate.sh`). Set an effort label on new issues. If your models differ, edit only the `model:` line in the four `issue-worker-*` agents.

`PROCESS_VERSION 7` · PR #750 · one cross-platform gate. `cargo xtask gate quick|batch|release|test <name>` (with `--dry-run`) and `cargo xtask decisions --version X.Y.Z` replace the logic of `scripts/gate.ps1`, `gate.sh` and `collect-decisions.*`. The scripts are now thin wrappers, so the old commands still work. AGENTS.md, the agents and the skills name `cargo xtask gate` as the one command. `xtask/` and `.cargo/config.toml` are now process files.

**Forks:** sync process files, adding the new paths: `git checkout upstream/main -- AGENTS.md .claude/agents .claude/skills .claude/PROCESS_VERSION scripts/gate.ps1 scripts/gate.sh scripts/collect-decisions.ps1 scripts/collect-decisions.sh xtask .cargo/config.toml`. If your fork's code is on a tag older than this, also add `"xtask"` to the workspace `members` in `Cargo.toml` in the same sync commit, or the wrappers fail. The `release.ps1` port is still open (#749).

`PROCESS_VERSION 8` · PR #751 · `cargo xtask release --version X.Y.Z --no-tag [--skip-gate] [--skip-build] [--installer] [--dry-run]` replaces `scripts/release.ps1`, which is now a thin wrapper. The cut runs on Windows, macOS, Linux and FreeBSD:
- **Phases:** the same ten phases as before.
- **Gate:** it runs the `gate release` tier.
- **Build:** only the product crates are built.
- **Zip:** it includes `NOTICE`, as `release.yml`'s does.
- **Packaging:** on Windows it still calls `sign.ps1` and `installer.ps1`. Elsewhere it uses `package-*.sh`; `--installer` is refused by name and signing is skipped.
- **Tags:** still made by hand on main after the release PR merges (step 4).
- **AGENTS.md:** the release step and the fix-only hand-test line name the new command. The hand-test runs on a scratch branch, not main.

#748 and #749 are closed. **Forks:** sync process files as in the issue body (`xtask` is already in the list since version 7).

`PROCESS_VERSION 9` · PR #753 · build pipeline unified on xtask:

- **CI:** `ci.yml` and `nightly.yml` call `cargo xtask gate batch|release` directly, and are still manual-only.
- **Docs:** `scripts/README.md` is rewritten around `cargo xtask`.
- **Process files:** the list now also includes `scripts/release.ps1` and `scripts/collect-decisions.ps1`/`.sh`.

**Forks:** sync process files with the full list in AGENTS.md: `git checkout upstream/main -- AGENTS.md .claude/agents .claude/skills .claude/PROCESS_VERSION xtask .cargo/config.toml scripts/gate.ps1 scripts/gate.sh scripts/release.ps1 scripts/collect-decisions.ps1 scripts/collect-decisions.sh`. The `release.yml` change ships with the next cut tag.

`PROCESS_VERSION 14` · PR #881 · a contributor's claim must be live. AGENTS.md "A claim comment is a claim" and review-prs step 4: a contributor's claim holds an issue only while there is an open PR by the claimant for it, a commit on the claimant's branch in the last 48 hours, or a comment by the claimant on the issue in the last 48 hours. Otherwise it is stale: it is not mirrored into a `claimed` label, and a label behind it is removed with a comment. A claim also ends when the claimant's last comment withdraws it, when the maintainer releases it, or when it has been released as stale - and an ended claim is never mirrored back from its old comment; only a new `claimed:` comment is a claim again. `P?` issues are never relabelled by the sweep. The 4 h rule for the owner account's own agents is unchanged. · A fork: pull the process files (the command in this issue's body). For contributors: a claim comment alone holds an issue for 48 hours; after that keep it live with an open PR, a recent commit on your branch, or a comment on the issue; renew a released claim with a new `claimed:` comment.

`PROCESS_VERSION 15` · PR #913 · build cycle (#900)

What changed:
- `cargo xtask gate` uses **sccache** as a shared compile cache when `sccache` is on PATH (sets `RUSTC_WRAPPER` and a 20G cache cap). An existing `RUSTC_WRAPPER` or `CAMCRAFT_NO_SCCACHE=1` wins; without sccache nothing changes.
- The dev profile is lighter: line-table debug info for our crates, none for dependencies, dependency `opt-level` 1 (was 2). The release profile is untouched. `--config profile.dev.debug=true` restores full debug info for a debugger session.
- Skills and agents (work-issue, resolve-conflicts, PR-reviewer): do **not** export `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` as an environment variable - sccache hashes `CARGO_*` variables, so with it set there are no cache hits across worktrees. Use each worktree's default `target/`.

What a fork must do: pull the process files (the command in this issue's body). Optional: install sccache (`cargo install sccache --locked` or your package manager) to get the shared cache. The first build after this lands rebuilds everything once (the profile changed).

Measured on Windows only (cold build 395 s -> 177 s with a warm cache, `target/` 43 % smaller). Linux and macOS are untested: #914 and #915 are open for contributors on those systems.

`PROCESS_VERSION 16` · PR #944 · compile cache: how agents use it, and the release build stays out of it (#935)

What changed:
- `work-issue`, `resolve-conflicts`, the `PR-reviewer` and `gate-runner` agents, and AGENTS.md now say: prefer `cargo xtask gate ...` (it turns the compile cache on); for a direct cargo call set `RUSTC_WRAPPER=sccache` only when `sccache` is on PATH (cargo fails if the wrapper is missing); never export `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`.
- `cargo xtask release` builds the shipped binary without a compiler wrapper even when `RUSTC_WRAPPER` or `CARGO_BUILD_RUSTC_WRAPPER` is set in the environment. The release gate tier may still use the cache.

What a fork must do: pull the process files (the command in this issue's body). A maintainer who wants every agent on their machine to use the cache can set `RUSTC_WRAPPER=sccache` in their own, not checked-in, settings; do not put it in `.cargo/config.toml` or the checked-in `.claude/settings.json` (it breaks machines without sccache).

`PROCESS_VERSION 29` · PR #1193 · **the priority scale changed: `P1`..`P9` replaces `P0`/`P1`/`P2`** (AGENTS.md, new section "Priorities"; skills `gh-issues`, `classify-effort`, `camcraft-mcp`). `P1` unsafe or wrong output · `P2` main broken · `P3` a bug users hit, with a workaround · `P4` work the maintainer asked for · `P5` owed agent/MCP surface and process fixes · `P6` accepted enhancements · `P7` polish · `P8` larger ideas · `P9` someday. Lowest number is picked first; no cut starts while any `P1` or `P2` is open; `P1`-`P3` are for defects only; an issue with no priority is triaged before any pick; `P?` is unchanged. **The meaning of `P1` flipped** (it was "a user hits it"; it is now the old `P0`). All 163 open issues of this repo were relabelled in one pass on 2026-11-12 (old `P0` -> `P1`; old `P1` bugs -> `P3`, maintainer-requested enhancements -> `P4`, MCP/process -> `P5`, others -> `P6`; old `P2` bugs -> `P7`, enhancements -> `P8`, or `P6` with an open PR); the `P0` label stays on closed issues as retired · **a fork must:** pull the process files (the command in this issue's body), create the labels `P3`..`P9`, and relabel its own open issues with the same mapping (the script is in `docs/decisions/1189-p1-p9-scale.md`; run it with `--dry-run` first).

`PROCESS_VERSION 31` · PR #1227 · **Refresh only at merge time** (maintainer's decision, 2026-11-12): a conflicting PR carries `conflicts` and is not refreshed until it is the next PR in a merge batch (or its author is pushing a review fix anyway) - the start-of-session refresh of every conflicting PR is superseded. A refresh that is only a merge of `main` with no hand edits (empty `git show --remerge-diff`) keeps its review; only a hand-resolved conflict gets a delta review, of the remerge-diff. **Only the repository owner's reviews count**: a `pr-reviewer` marker or a `merge-ready` label from another account is not a review. New: `cargo xtask merge-plan <PR>...` plans a merge order by simulating the merges, and `cargo xtask merge-plan --delta <PR> --reviewed <sha>` classifies a moved head (SAME / MECHANICAL / DELTA / NEW CODE). One batch gate per merge batch. · **What a fork must do:** pull the process files (the command in this issue's body); stop refreshing every conflicting PR at session start; do not post the `pr-reviewer` marker or set `merge-ready` on your own PRs - a pre-check is a plain comment.

@mkinney - heads-up ahead of PROCESS_VERSION 32. Rule change, decided by the maintainer in the question dialog on 2026-11-12 (later the same day as PROCESS_VERSION 31): **"Any collaborator review counts"** and, on who may merge, **"Both collaborators"**. His words: "everyone counts. everyone needs to get merged, mkinney and i are coolaboration across the world on the same code base". So the owner-only rule of PROCESS_VERSION 31 is superseded: a review marker and a `merge-ready` label count when a COLLABORATOR (an account with write access; today NeoTech, mkinney, dudedagger42) posted them - on their own PRs too, as long as the review was done by an agent that did not write the change (AGENTS.md's existing rule) - and any collaborator's session may merge reviewed PRs with the `merge-ready` skill; release cuts stay with the maintainer. A marker or label from a non-collaborator still does not count. The process text follows in the PR for #1320 (PROCESS_VERSION 32); the rule applies from now.

In practice: my earlier notes on your PRs asking you not to post the marker or set `merge-ready` on your own PRs no longer apply. Labels I removed under the old rule I will not re-add in bulk - set them again where your reviewer cleared the current head. Where our reviewer has posted requested changes on a head, please treat those as open until addressed; they were real defects each time.

`PROCESS_VERSION 32` · PR #1321 · **This reverses part of version 31, issued earlier the same day.**

- **Any collaborator's review counts** (maintainer, 2026-11-12: "Any collaborator review counts"; who may merge: "Both collaborators"; "everyone counts. everyone needs to get merged, mkinney and i are coolaboration across the world on the same code base"). A `pr-reviewer` / `review-cost` marker and a `merge-ready` label count when a collaborator (an account with write access) posted them - on their own PRs too, provided the review was done by an agent that did not write the change. Version 31's "only the repository owner's reviews count" is superseded. A marker or label from a non-collaborator still does not count, and a non-collaborator's PR still waits for the maintainer.
- **Any collaborator's session may merge** reviewed PRs, fixes and features alike. Release cuts and tags stay with the maintainer.
- **A requested change stays open until addressed**: a `merge-ready` label or a "ready" review from another collaborator on the same head does not override a review that requests changes. Such a PR is a disagreement - it is reported, not merged, and no agent removes either label; the two collaborators settle it on the PR.
- **New skill `/merge-ready`** (`.claude/skills/merge-ready/`): lists the `merge-ready` PRs, plans the order with `cargo xtask merge-plan`, asks the person running it yes/no per PR, merges the cleanly-merging wave first and then refreshes and merges the rest one at a time. It never merges an unapproved PR and never refreshes a PR that is not next in the batch.
- **`cargo xtask merge-plan` is deterministic**: the same PR heads and base always give the same plan (every choice ends in a tie-break on the PR number); the plan prints the base sha and each head sha; `--json` gives the same plan to other tools.

**What a fork must do:** pull the process files (the command in this issue's body). Collaborators: you may set `merge-ready` and post review markers on PRs your reviewer agent cleared, and merge with `/merge-ready`; the notes on individual PRs asking you not to are withdrawn.
